brief.headline: Move from paying-on-delivery to normal 30-day credit and free up ₹44.91 L of our cash — their own cash is stuck for 75d, longer than rivals' 30d, so they'll value being paid faster.

priceAsk.summary: Hold price or ask for a 3–4% cut if we move to faster payment (15 days instead of 30).
priceAsk.target: Around ₹240/kg (vs market typical ₹250/kg) if we pay in 15 days
priceAsk.basis: Open-market asking price for pharma sachet laminate is ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg — our price sits at the top of that fair band. Their cash is stuck for 75d vs similar firms' 30d, and they borrow at 6.7%, so paying them 15 days faster (instead of the standard 30) is worth roughly 3–4% to them. Trade that speed for a small price cut.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move to 30-day credit as the baseline; offer 15-day credit only in exchange for a 3–4% price cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Moving to 30 days frees up ₹44.91 L of our cash; stopping at 15 days still frees ₹22.45 L.

brief.financialLeverage: They're a ₹4491.70 Cr global packaging giant — healthy operations (they make ₹363.93 Cr free cash each year) but carrying debt of 1.09x their own cash and sitting in the grey zone for financial distress (Altman Z 2.15). Their cash is stuck for 75d, much longer than similar firms' 30d, so they value faster payment. We're tiny — just 0.12% of their sales — so on our own we have little pull. But they keep only 5.4% profit vs rivals' 10.2%, meaning price cuts hurt them more. Win on payment terms and delivery, not just price, and line up a second source (Huhtamaki or UFLEX, both already FDC suppliers) to show we're serious.

evidence.point: Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
They borrow money at about this rate
They keep less profit than rivals
Market asking price for pharma sachet laminate
A lot of their deliveries get reversed or returned

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter, already a tiny FDC supplier — a proven second source for laminate sachets (₹2611.64 Cr revenue, health C 59/100).

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant doing both film and conversion — can second-source laminates at scale (₹16492.00 Cr revenue, health C 46/100).

risks: They're in the grey zone for financial stress (Altman Z 2.15) and carry severe legal cases — watch supply continuity and have Huhtamaki or UFLEX ready as backup.
We're only 0.12% of their business, so they may not move much on price unless we bundle volume, commit longer, or show a credible second source.
22% of deliveries are reversed or returned — fix quality and paperwork issues before they eat into any saving we negotiate.
They keep only 5.4% profit vs rivals' 10.2% — pushing too hard on price may backfire; focus the ask on payment terms and delivery performance.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to standard 30-day credit to free up cash on our side — and if you'd value being paid even faster, say 15 days, we can talk about a small price adjustment in return.
